questions.question: List out the application of layering.
questions.solution_html:
• Applicationoflayering
  •  Propagation ofwoody perennial plants
  •  Multiplication ofplants with poorrooting ability
  •  Truetotype propagation
  •  Early bearing of crops
  •  Propagation ofclimbing plants
  • Seed Coat: Outerprotective layer (testaand tegmen).
  • Nursery Practices: Includes site selection (well-drained, sunny), soil sterilization
  • and bed preparation (raised beds). Proper sowing depth and spacing are vital to prevent
  • overcrowding.
  • Sexual Propagation (Seeds): Involves the fusion of male and female gametes. It
  • promotes genetic diversity butmay result inoffspring different from theparent.
questions.final_answer: promotes genetic diversity butmay result inoffspring different from theparent

questions.question: List out detached scion method of grafting.
questions.solution_html:
• Detached Scion Grafting: A method where the scion is completely separated from
  • the mother plant before being joined to the rootstock. Examples include wedge
  • grafting, tongue grafting, and cleft grafting.
questions.final_answer: grafting, tongue grafting, and cleft grafting

questions.question: How plant propagation helps in disease free plant production?
questions.solution_html:
• Disease-Free Plant Production: Propagation helps through meristem
  • culture (which eliminates viruses because the growing tip is often pathogen-free) and
  • byusing certified disease-free motherplants orresistant rootstocks.
questions.final_answer: byusing certified disease-free motherplants orresistant rootstocks

questions.question: Define line sowing (drilling).
questions.solution_html:
• Line Sowing (Drilling): The process of sowing seeds in continuous lines at a
  • controlled depth and uniform spacing, usually done using a seed drill or by hand in
  • furrows.

questions.question: Write a short note on compound layering.
questions.solution_html:
• Compound Layering: Also known as serpentine layering. A long branch is
  • alternately covered with soil and left exposed at intervals. Roots form at every buried
  • node, allowing multipleplants to beproduced from asingle shoot.
questions.final_answer: node, allowing multipleplants to beproduced from asingle shoot

questions.question: Describe the different steps involved in seed preparation before sowing.
questions.solution_html:
• Seed Preparation
  • Extraction:Removingseeds from thefruit or pod.
  • Drying:Reducing moistureto ensure longevity.
  • Cleaning/Grading:Removing debris and selecting heavy, healthy seeds.
  • Seed Treatment: Using fungicides to prevent disease or techniques like scarification to
  • break dormancy.

questions.question: Write a note on the importance of plant propagation in agriculture.
questions.solution_html:
• Importance ofplantpropagationin agriculture
  •  Ensures ContinuousSupply ofPlantingMaterial
  •  Helps Maintain Genetic Purity and Uniformity
  •  Enables Improvement ofCrop Varieties
  •  Conserves Eliteand RareGermplasm
  •  Facilitates Rapid Multiplication ofPlants
  •  Essential forPerennial and Horticultural Crops
  •  Enhances Disease-Free PlantProduction
  •  SupportsCommercial Agriculture and Nurseries

questions.question: Explain the importance of seed selection in horticulture.
questions.solution_html:
• DEVELOPMENT
  • Development includes all the changes in a plant from the germination of seed to senescence.
  • Plants during their growth and development show different responses tothe environmental
  • conditionsand develop different structures. This ability isknown as plasticity.
  • Example
  •  Heterophylly is seen in thecotton, coriander and buttercup plants.
  •  In cotton and coriander plants, the leaves in juvenile and adult plants are different
  • morphologically
